terms.meaning: Whether a number is even or odd.
A square grid where every row, column and diagonal has the same sum, called the magic sum.
1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13… where each number is the sum of the two before it. They are also called Virahanka-Fibonacci numbers.

items.name: Adding and subtracting
items.formula: Even ± even and odd ± odd are even. Even ± odd is odd.

items.name: Adding many odd numbers
items.formula: An even count gives even. An odd count gives odd.
items.example: 1 + 3 + 5 = 9 is odd, so five odd numbers can never add up to 30.

items.name: Two numbers in a row
items.example: Ages one year apart cannot add up to 112.

items.name: Multiplying
items.formula: Odd × odd is odd. Anything else is even.

items.name: The nth even and odd numbers
Magic sum using 1 to 9
items.formula: The total is 45, so each row adds up to 15

items.name: Making a new magic square
items.formula: Add or multiply every number by the same number
items.example: Add 2 to each number: the magic sum becomes 15 + 3 × 2 = 21.

items.name: The next number
items.formula: Add the two numbers before it

items.name: Even and odd in the sequence

mistakes.text: Odd + odd is even, but odd + odd + odd is odd. Count how many odd numbers there are.
If one factor is even, the whole product is even. 3 × 5 × 2 = 30.
In a magic square, check the diagonals too, not only the rows and columns.
